about: Opening-line patterns for Reels. Each has a spoken template, a worked example, a card for the screen (read before it is heard), when to use it, how it usually fails, and a case-insensitive regex so igos can name the pattern in hooks it finds in the wild. Patterns are tried in the order listed: most specific first.
principles: Two hooks run at once: the sentence you say and the card on screen. Write them separately. The card is shorter.
Start at the most interesting sentence. Delete everything you would normally say before it.
Give the viewer something countable: a number, a name, a time, a place.
Promise one thing and pay it off before the halfway mark.
If a competitor could say the line word for word, it is not your hook yet.

families.proof: Leads with a result, a number or a receipt.
families.tension: Leads with a conflict, a mistake or a contradiction.
families.curiosity: Opens a gap the viewer wants closed.
families.utility: Promises a usable thing: a list, a template, a shortcut.
families.story: Drops the viewer into a moment already in motion.

patterns.name: Price of a Mistake
patterns.example: Skipping a deposit cost me $6,400 last spring.
patterns.use_when: You need trust quickly. Viewers stay for the person who admits the loss.
patterns.failure_mode: A vague price. 'It cost me so much' gives the viewer nothing to picture.

patterns.name: Before / After Number
patterns.example: Our reply time went from two days to nine minutes in one week.
patterns.use_when: You have a clean transformation with two numbers.
patterns.failure_mode: Numbers the viewer cannot check against their own life. Pick a metric they also track.

patterns.name: The Receipt
patterns.template: This {artifact} made {result}. Here is what is in it.
patterns.example: This one-page brief booked us eleven calls. Here's what's in it.
patterns.use_when: The thing itself can be shown on screen: a doc, a dashboard, a message.
patterns.failure_mode: Showing the result but hiding the artifact. Show it or pick another pattern.

patterns.name: Borrowed Result
patterns.template: {Named person or business} did {surprising result} with {small input}.
patterns.example: A bakery in Pune got 40,000 views with a phone and a tripod.
patterns.use_when: You are teaching from someone else's win and can name them.
patterns.failure_mode: Anonymous case studies. 'A client of mine' is weaker than a named place.

patterns.name: Hard Stat
patterns.example: Eight in ten people watch your Reel with the sound off.
patterns.use_when: A real statistic reframes a habit. Cite it in the caption.
patterns.failure_mode: An unsourced number. If you cannot link it, do not say it.

patterns.name: Wrong Order
patterns.template: You're doing {task} in the wrong order.
patterns.example: You're writing the caption before the hook. That's backwards.
patterns.use_when: The fix is a sequence change, which is easy to show and easy to try.
patterns.failure_mode: No new order revealed. Name the right order within five seconds.

patterns.name: Quit This
patterns.example: Quit posting at 9 a.m. Your audience is asleep in another time zone.
patterns.use_when: The viewer recognises the habit in themselves.
patterns.failure_mode: Attacking a habit nobody has.

patterns.name: The Flip
patterns.example: Posting every day is bad advice for a three-person business.
patterns.use_when: You disagree with something everyone repeats and can back it up.
patterns.failure_mode: Disagreeing with a straw man. Quote the actual advice.
patterns.regex: \b(?:is|are) (?:wrong|a lie|a myth|overrated|bad advice|a trap|dead|outdated)\b|\bunpopular opinion\b|\bhot take\b|\beveryone says\b|\bthey told you\b

patterns.name: The Quiet Part
patterns.example: What nobody says about going viral: your inbox fills with spam, not clients.
patterns.use_when: You have an insider truth the viewer has not heard.
patterns.failure_mode: A truth that is already common knowledge.

patterns.name: Pointed Why
patterns.example: Why do your best posts get the fewest saves?
patterns.use_when: The viewer has noticed the puzzle themselves.
patterns.failure_mode: A question with an obvious answer. If they can answer it, they scroll.

patterns.name: Hidden Reason
patterns.example: The real reason your Reels stall at 300 views is the first frame, not the hook.
patterns.use_when: You can name one cause and show it.
patterns.failure_mode: Five reasons. The pattern promises one.

patterns.name: Found Out
patterns.example: I found out our top competitor writes every caption on a phone in a car.
patterns.use_when: You discovered something by looking closely.
patterns.failure_mode: A reveal that is not surprising once said.

patterns.name: I Tested It
patterns.example: I replied to every comment within ten minutes for 30 days. Reach doubled.
patterns.use_when: You ran a real experiment and have the number.
patterns.failure_mode: An experiment with no number at the end.

patterns.name: Copy This
patterns.example: Copy the four-line DM that got me three podcast invites.
patterns.use_when: You can give away a literal template on screen.
patterns.failure_mode: Teasing the template and gating it behind a comment without showing any of it.

patterns.name: Things I'd Never Do
patterns.template: {Number} things I'll never do again as a {role}.
patterns.example: Three things I'll never do again as a wedding photographer.
patterns.use_when: You have scars from real practice.
patterns.failure_mode: Items that are obvious ('never be unprofessional').

patterns.name: Numbered Shortcut
patterns.example: Three caption edits that took our saves from 12 to 90.
patterns.use_when: The items are short enough to land one per beat.
patterns.failure_mode: Seven items in a 20-second Reel. Three is the ceiling for most.

patterns.name: How I Did X
patterns.example: How I got to 10,000 followers without showing my face.
patterns.use_when: The 'without' removes the viewer's main objection.
patterns.failure_mode: Leaving out the 'without'. Without the constraint it is a generic how-to.

patterns.name: If You Are...
patterns.example: If you sell anything over $500, put the price in your third slide.
patterns.use_when: You want to self-select a narrow audience on purpose.
patterns.failure_mode: A situation so broad it filters nobody: 'If you want to grow'.
patterns.regex: ^\s*(?:if you|if your|for anyone who|this is for)\b

patterns.name: The Extreme
patterns.example: The cheapest marketing that ever worked for us cost $14.
patterns.use_when: You genuinely have a record or an outlier.
patterns.failure_mode: Hyperbole you cannot defend. The comments will check.

patterns.name: Mid-Scene
patterns.example: It's 11 p.m., the launch is at nine, and the checkout page is broken.
patterns.use_when: You have a real moment with stakes and a clock.
patterns.failure_mode: Setting the scene with no complication. Start at the problem.

patterns.name: Confession
patterns.example: For two years I priced by guessing what the client could afford.
patterns.use_when: The admission sets up a lesson the viewer needs.
patterns.failure_mode: A humble-brag dressed as a confession.

patterns.name: This vs That
patterns.example: Carousel vs Reel for a product launch: here's what our numbers said.
patterns.use_when: The viewer is choosing between two things right now.
patterns.failure_mode: Ending on 'it depends'. Pick a side for a stated case.

patterns.name: POV Card
patterns.example: POV: the client says 'quick tweak' at 5:58 on a Friday.
patterns.use_when: Humour or recognition carries the Reel more than information.
patterns.failure_mode: A POV that needs explaining.

patterns.name: Warning
patterns.example: Before you boost a post, check whether it was 3:4. Those can't be promoted.
patterns.use_when: There is a real, specific risk in a routine action.
patterns.failure_mode: Fear with no check attached.
